classification.difficultyReason: Solve an angle equation and use the converse of the co-interior angle property to justify both pairs of parallel sides.

content.prompt: Show that this shape is a parallelogram. Clearly justify your answer.

spec.description: Unshaded slanted quadrilateral with four interior angle arcs and algebraic labels; no parallel or equal-side marks. Source grey strokes are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: Clockwise from upper left, angles are (3x−5)°, (4x+10)°, (2x+20)° and (5x−15)°. Drawing coordinates reproduce topology and approximate proportions, not specified measurements.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied angle expressions are visible; no solved values or parallel-side conclusions appear.

answer.short: $x=25$. Clockwise from the upper left, the angles are $70^{\circ},110^{\circ},70^{\circ},110^{\circ}$. Adjacent angles sum to $180^{\circ}$, proving both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
answer.worked:
The interior angles of a quadrilateral sum to $360^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}(3x-5)+(4x+10)+(2x+20)+(5x-15)&=360\\14x+10&=360\\14x&=350\\x&=25\end{align*}$$
Clockwise from the upper left:
$$\begin{align*}3x-5&=3(25)-5=70\\4x+10&=4(25)+10=110\\2x+20&=2(25)+20=70\\5x-15&=5(25)-15=110\end{align*}$$
The top and bottom sides are parallel because the two interior angles on the left side sum to $70^{\circ}+110^{\circ}=180^{\circ}$. The left and right sides are parallel because the two interior angles on the top side also sum to $180^{\circ}$, using the converse of the co-interior angle property. Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, so the shape is a parallelogram.
